summary: The note describes a growing movement toward locally sourced ingredients in regional cuisine across the US, driven by sustainability and community values. It profiles chefs, farmers, cooking schools, consumers, foragers, apps and government policies that support local food networks. It concludes that local sourcing could produce more diverse regional cuisines and more resilient food systems.
one_line: Locally sourced ingredients are reviving regional cuisine through chefs, farm partnerships, schools, consumers, technology and policy, pointing toward more sustainable food systems.
key_facts: Chef Emily Rosenthal has, since October 2023, run a restaurant in Asheville, North Carolina that operates exclusively on a locally-sourced menu.
Rosenthal says "Local sourcing is more than a trend—it's about community, economy, and ultimately, taste."

In November 2023, farmer Jonah Henderson of Henderson Family Farms agreed to supply 'The Root Café' in Little Rock, Arkansas with year-round organic root vegetables in exchange for shared marketing initiatives.
Henderson describes the arrangement with The Root Café as "essentially co-branding" and a symbiotic relationship.
Partnerships between restaurants and farms are also incubating community-supported agriculture (CSA) programs, where individuals invest directly in local farms and receive regular boxes of produce.
The San Francisco Culinary Institute adopted a "locally sourced first" policy in January 2024, teaching students to use the bounty of Northern California.
Recent graduate Maria Lopez said the education taught her to understand where ingredients come from and the impact of her choices.
Rachel Fine, manager of the Green City Market in Chicago, says customers now ask farmers about crop rotations, pesticide use and heirloom seeds.
Apps and online marketplaces connecting consumers with local food sources have proliferated since the late 2020s and help homesteaders turn excess harvest into local commerce.
Expert forager Lee Nguyen leads educational foraging in the parks of Seattle, finding mushrooms, berries and edible greens.
In February 2024, chef Aarav Singh of 'Spice Roots' in Boulder, Colorado blended his Indian heritage with Rocky Mountain terroir, using local game and vegetables with traditional Indian spices.
Cities like New York and Los Angeles have urban garden initiatives and subsidies for local producers to strengthen local food networks.
The note predicts broader adoption could lead to more resilient food systems less reliant on distant, large-scale agriculture.
